Incremental Static Regeneration, or ISR, allows pages to be updated in the background as traffic flows to them while they are being rendered by Next.js. This feature combines the benefits of static and dynamic rendering.

To create an API endpoint in Next.js, you can use the `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, or `DELETE` methods provided by Express. These methods allow you to perform CRUD (create, read, update, and delete) operations on your API endpoints.

For example, if you want to create a new user, you can send a `POST` request to the `/api/users` endpoint with the user's data in the body of the request. This will trigger the function in the `pages/api/users.js` file, which can then use the Express methods to perform the desired operation on the database.

To summarize, creating an API endpoint in Next.js involves:

1. Creating a new folder called `pages/api` inside your Next.js project.
2. Inside this folder, create a new JavaScript file for each API endpoint you want to create (e.g., `pages/api/users.js`).
3. Use the Express methods (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, or `DELETE`) provided by Next.js to perform CRUD operations on your API endpoints.
4. Test your API endpoints using a tool like Postman or cURL.

The answer is _document.js differs from _app.js in the following ways:

1. `_document.js` has its own lifecycle methods, such as `getStaticProps`, which are not available in `_app.js`. These methods allow you to define how data is fetched and rendered for each page.
2. `_document.js` allows custom HTML and `<body>` tags, as well as custom meta tags for every page. This means that you can add your own HTML elements and attributes to the document head or body, and also define custom meta tags like title, description, or keywords.
3. `_document.js` is executed before rendering the component tree, while `_app.js` is executed after the components have been rendered. This means that in `_document.js`, you can define how the initial HTML markup should look, while in `_app.js`, you can define the layout and structure of your app.

In summary, `_document.js` allows for more control over the HTML and meta tags of each page, while `_app.js` provides a way to customize the layout and structure of the component tree.
